chapters.title: How You Get There — Meditation and the Formless Realm

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now, with the form realm — and we're going to talk about the formless realm in a second, which is above the form realm — how do you get there? The form realm is the highest peak of all existing form. That's why I have this picture of the Greek gods, the artistry of the classical West. But this doesn't get anywhere close to the perfection of what happens in the form realm.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: How do you get there? Basically, it's different types of meditation. If you get to shamatha, and you're meditating very, very well, single-pointedly, you can go deeper and deeper into shamatha. Each of those levels of concentration also removes your awareness of the body and the world around you entirely. So the meditation gets subtler and subtler. The cause to get there is incredibly subtle and deep meditation. And then if your meditation gets even better, even more subtle, that results in the formless realm.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: The formless realm is like a picture of space. But it's not space like you get on a rocket and go out between Neptune and Pluto. It's simply where you are — you're born in this place, right where you are, but the form body is absent. You have all the other parts of the mind — awareness, consciousness, feeling. Your body just has a subtle existence.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And the formless realm — suk-me-kham [GZUGS MED KHAMS] — next slide, Brian — has four levels. Each of them is more and more subtle. It's almost like being completely under anesthesia — you almost lose your entire awareness of anything.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So there are four levels. The first is Limitless Space [NAM MKHA' MTHA' YAS]. The next one up is called Limitless Awareness [RNAM SHES MTHA' YAS]. The next level is Nothingness [CI YANG MED] — simply, nothing at all. And then the last level is called the Peak of Existence [SRID RTSE].

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Each of these levels has different names, different colors, and different meditations that get you there — and generally the name of the meditation is similar to the name of the realm itself. So your awareness goes up and up, the meditations become subtler and subtler as a cause, and they result in birth in one of the 17 levels of the form realm or the four levels of the formless realm. Super fascinating — I can tell you're all excited.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: One more thing. What distinguishes the form realm from the formless realm, or from the lower realms? It's the same kind of definition as the others. There are no physical objects in the formless realm, but there are particular objects that the mind holds onto, which develop certain kinds of mental afflictions. It's not a physical object — but we call it an object because anything the mind focuses on is called an object.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So imagine you're living in a world that's just limitless space, or limitless awareness, or nothingness. There's not a physical object there, but your mind is still thinking of something. So it creates some kind of little mental affliction. Okay — now I'm done with the boring stuff.

chapters.title: Why It All Matters — Reaching the Level That Sees Emptiness

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So why are we talking about 17 different meditations that create the form realm and four different meditations that create the formless realm — 21 meditations in total?

paragraphs.speaker: Ray
paragraphs.text: Because seeing emptiness directly requires reaching a specific level.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Because in order to see emptiness directly, you need to reach certain particular levels. Damn — I should have offered you $100. That's a $100 answer. That's exactly what I wanted to get to. Good job, Ray.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But the first answer I want to get to is this: when you get really good at meditating, it begins to feel really good — and you can get stuck there. You can be planting the causes to be born in one of these places, which frankly is really nice. Being in the form realm and the formless realm — those are really lovely rebirths. In the form realm, your body is perfect. No pain. Everything you do just brings out bliss and happiness. Everything you need is there — great relationships, great food, great sex, all the time. It's not even that you need any of those things; it's just enjoyable. Everything is enjoyable.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then what happens? Like everything else, eventually those seeds wear out. It takes a tremendous amount of good karma to be born in a place where there's mainly no suffering at all. No pain. You don't have to go searching for food. You have all the companionship and all the pleasure you need. You don't get lonely. You don't get depressed. You don't have childhood trauma. You don't have any of that. Sounds like a great place for me — my back would never hurt, never any jet lag, I don't run over my toe in the grocery store, free eggs, all the free eggs you want.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But then that karma has to wear out. And the end of life is absolutely terrible in the form realm. Your body begins to rot. Does everyone know that experience? In Taiwan you have organic waste separated — but the food waste still stinks, right? Well, it's infinitely worse than that. You know how there are some people who refuse to take showers, or never wear deodorant, and you walk by and you're like, "Can you go over there?" Infinitely worse than that. So bad that everyone keeps their distance from you. They're so repulsed by your smell that they just walk away from you. And you finally experience loneliness — for the first time. And then what happens? You die. And what comes out next? Another form-realm being?

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: No.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: No. Because you just used up all of your good karma. The only thing that comes out then is very bad seeds — probably hell-realm seeds. So sure, you might have millions of years of pleasurable existence, but it can't last forever.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So that was the first answer to that question. Learning to meditate and doing those things — sure, it can create that for you. Wonderful, great. But it's not sustainable. The $100 answer — well, he got 1,000 NTD for it — is that what we're actually striving to do is reach a certain level of meditation, but not go beyond it. We're looking to get our mind into the very first part of the form realm's causal meditations — a type of concentration that's incredible. Because at that level, it becomes the platform where you can see emptiness directly. Of course the microphone went off when I said something cool. You want to get to that certain level, but not beyond it — because if you go beyond it, you're just creating the causes to be a being that's not going to live on. It's just going to be samsara.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Let me say one thing: we actually don't need to worry about this too much. Does anybody have shamatha in their meditation for one full hour? Be honest — raise your hand, real high. Tyler's laughing. Marina's laughing. Ken's laughing. If you don't even have shamatha yet, don't worry about it. But it's good to know — because if you do get to shamatha, and it is possible with the right seeds, usually in retreat… Retreat isn't the cause of good meditation, by the way. You have to plant the seeds to make retreat work. We'll talk about this a little later.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: To get to shamatha requires a tremendous amount of seeds — to get yourself to that first form level takes extraordinary good karma. And then you use that platform to trigger the direct perception of emptiness — which in some way was triggered by seeing the pot on the stove. The way to get there is perhaps to study with someone who's done it before. And one of those beings that I know, that I've met, might be teaching those things in the course called the Bridge to the Diamond Way. Maybe the meditations he's giving are the ones creating the seeds for you, so that when you get to that level of meditation, you can hopefully have a chance to pop out into the direct perception of emptiness. There are a lot of components — maybe 16 of them — and each has different seeds to plant.

chapters.title: Meditation Starts Off the Cushion — Delete the Angry Message

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But how do you get to a place where you can even meditate well enough, be focused enough, to do those things? Your meditation practice starts off the cushion. It starts with how you treat other people. That person who irritates you — how do you treat them? Are they your enemy? Or are they your source of good meditation? Maybe they're your opportunity to plant a seed so you can have good meditation. Instead of being irritated and thinking, "I can't believe you're treating me like this," you can be like, "Oh, thanks for giving me the opportunity to have better meditation."

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm getting lots of messages right now — you know the expression, "everyone and their mother"? Everyone and their mother is writing me right now, because they want an invitation to Dragonshead. It's just an expression, meaning everybody. But I didn't make those decisions — I'm kind of the messenger. I have someone who's really being annoying right now, writing everybody, twisting things and confusing things to get people into Dragonshead. And I could get irritated. But what happens if I get irritated? I go meditate, and then I'll have terrible meditation. Or I could be like, "All right, you're just giving me the opportunity to be patient" — thank you for giving me this chance to have good meditation.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I am the master of writing the best answer and then deleting it. Understand? Don't send the email when you first write the response. Whatever you want to say — on Telegram, or online, or whatever chat and media you use — just delete it. Write your response, and you know when you're afflicted, right? Because you just wrote this big thing about how you're right and they're the asshole. Just delete it. It doesn't matter how right you are in your mind — just delete it. This goes for a lot of you online too. Write it, and then delete it. And then walk away.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Because if you send that and the person reads it — even the fact of writing it is probably not the best idea, but sometimes we have to recognize that we're irritated in order to not be irritated. So keep a personal journal. See it as a purification, and burn it up. Delete, delete, delete. Then come back later when your mind is cooler. I did that three times this morning. The person is now writing Geshe Michael because they didn't like my answer. They wrote Geshe Michael, I gave the answer; then they wrote me again, I gave them the same answer; then they wrote Geshe Michael again with the same question — as though the answer is going to be different. And I was just like, "No, no." Delete, delete, delete. "I understand where you're coming from. This makes a lot of sense. Let me talk to Geshe Michael and see what we can do."

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Take a deep breath in. Hold. Exhale. Inhale the goodness, exhale some of the garbage. If you don't do that, you're never going to get shamatha. One moment of this kind of affliction can destroy six months of your meditation. So what's more important — writing that message? If you're online, that's what I typed in the chat. When you're writing those responses, it's just gibberish. It's garbage. Or, if you want to ruin your meditation for six months, or for the rest of your lifetime, and make it impossible to advance — okay, just be angry. Just be self-righteous. Go, enjoy, have fun with that. Be the Donald Trump on Truth Social, writing all this garbage about people. Kind of funny — in this particular class from 25 years ago, Geshe Michael mentions Donald Trump, and they mention him as a type of — I'll talk about it later.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But if you really, truly want to see emptiness directly, you have to take care of your irritation and anger. The number of people in this universe who can irritate you in the desire realm is every existing person in the universe. They all have that possibility. As they say in the Hunger Games — "may the odds be ever in your favor." And that movie is all about how they select 20 kids and they all kill each other, and only one wins. The odds are not in our favor.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Which movie is that?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: The Hunger Games. But you have to battle that. You have to delete your responses. The automatic responses you have — you have to begin deleting them. I had a dream last night that I was riding on a big dinosaur, a Tyrannosaurus rex. I was riding it like a horse — it had reins, and I was holding on and guiding it. That's what you have to do with your mental afflictions. It's like an uncontrollable Tyrannosaurus rex. You've got to control that stuff. You've got to tame it — dul-wa {? ['DUL BA']} is in the Vinaya; you have to tame it. If you want to reach those higher goals, you have to delete the angry message.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: "But what if I'm right?" That feeling that you're right is the first thing that needs to be deleted — because behind it is a Tyrannosaurus rex, pretending not to be. Get it? Okay, that was a long description. Holy — it's already 5:20.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, so I went on a little trip. Now, in the desire realm — we just took care of the upper realms. We're not going to spend more than a class on those, because getting there requires intensely awesome meditation. We're going to focus mostly on the desire realm, because that's where we claim to spend most of our time.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Slide nine, Brian. So, the lowest realm — the hell realms. This is the hell being, a nyel-wa [DMYAL BA]. Do they look like that? I don't know. But I think if we can imagine it, it probably exists. This is the lowest realm. It's just tremendous suffering — either you're inflicting pain on others, or you're having pain inflicted on you, constantly.
